title: docs: P104 side-correction scope map (results by premise, shared 328/9 budget line; no new kappa)
body:
## What this adds

This adds a single file, `docs/research/p104-side-correction-scope-map.md`. It is a navigation map for the revision-4 `p104-side-correction` card, in the style of `docs/research/complex-decoder-scope-map.md`. No new mathematics, no review dispositions, no κ or selected-frontier change.

Fourteen PRs and threads now work on the same `I-G/2` completion of the native P104 channel, many from the last two hours. The map pins each to its exact head and records three things: which premise it fixes (cut, transports kept, storage, frame paths, producer, precision), what it concludes, and what it explicitly leaves outside.

Sources covered:
- open PRs https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2082, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2083, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2089, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2090, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2096, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2113 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2127;
- the channel in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1972 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1991;
- discussions https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2080, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2092, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2107, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2121 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2131.

It follows revision 4's request to "summarize which common premise has been tested and what the next search would change".

## The one derived observation

CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2082 and CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2083 price completions under the same conditional coverage contract (s = N = 9, m = 73, W = 832, unchanged idle requirements). Under it, a correction with no creditable progress keeps the zero-saving moment at or below one only if it adds at most **328/9 ≈ 36.4 rank units per call**. CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2082 states the same slack. Every route covered so far is either infeasible (the 8-array cuts) or needs at least 96 added transports. The constructions and candidates pay 208.

So within the shared premises the route is closed. Only two kinds of change remain open:
1. replacing or fusing original transports, or adding new frame paths (live claims in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2121 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2131);
2. a coverage interface that credits added transports.

The map also notes that closing the 96..208 gap doesn't matter under the retained contract.

## Checks

- The doc's Python snippet reproduces the cited moments exactly with `fractions`: 7659/7592 at 96, 1917/1898 at 104, 7785/7592 at 208, 7551/7592 uncorrected, and the 328/9 slack. Constants are taken from the PR bodies, not from fresh package replays.
- Both relative links resolve. There are no bare PR references.
- `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 65 tests OK (3 skipped).
- All nine PR heads were re-checked unchanged at 20:25 UTC. Canonical main is still `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4).
- The overlap refresh (389 open PRs, 796 discussion records, complete pagination) found no other scope map. One P104 claim appeared at 20:17 UTC (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2131) and is included.

**Not checked:** I did not replay any cited package, so the open-PR entries are their authors' claims as stated. The map is a dated snapshot and will go stale as these PRs change; each entry gives its head for that reason.

## Task

- Drawn: complex-mechanisms, card `p104-side-correction`, chooser nonce `babf7d7d03bf6b191d708ecb1d52d2aa`, base `0fdd7d82`.
- Scope **changed** to consolidation, because every concrete sub-question was already claimed or in an open PR.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18933452.

## Credit

All results belong to their authors: Rohan Arun, Chafik Boukhalfa, Adam Gall, David Arias, Jeremy Diviney, Ross Richardson, 1337isnot1337, Jose Manuel and the credited lineage. The coverage contract sources are Dominik Scholz's paired-chain model, Sagar Thakrar (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012) and Douglas Colkitt (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240). Authors: corrections to how I summarized your scope are welcome.

Prepared by Aaron Wang / navinor, with help from Claude Code. Apache-2.0. Not requesting merge; selected frontier unchanged.
